reference_source: OpenStax University Physics Volume 1, Chapters 5-6 (Newton's Laws of Motion; Applications of Newton's Laws)

questions.prompt: State Newton's First Law of Motion and explain what is meant by an 'inertial frame of reference'. Give one real-world example.

criteria.description: Correct statement of the law of inertia (no net force -> no change in velocity)
Correct explanation of inertial reference frame
Valid real-world example correctly tied to the law

questions.prompt: A 5 kg block rests on a frictionless horizontal surface. A horizontal force of 20 N is applied. Using Newton's Second Law, find the acceleration of the block. Show your free-body diagram and working.

criteria.description: Correct free-body diagram showing applied force, weight, normal force
Correct equation setup: F_net = ma applied along horizontal axis
Correct substitution and final numeric answer (a = 4 m/s^2) with units

questions.prompt: Explain Newton's Third Law using the example of a swimmer pushing off a wall. Why do the two equal and opposite forces not cancel each other out?

criteria.description: Correct statement: forces are equal in magnitude, opposite in direction
Correct application to swimmer/wall example, correctly identifying action-reaction pair
Correct explanation that forces act on different systems/objects, so they don't cancel

questions.prompt: A 10 kg box is pulled along a rough horizontal floor by a rope at a tension of 40 N, with a coefficient of kinetic friction of 0.2. Find the acceleration of the box. (Use g = 9.8 m/s^2)

criteria.description: Correct free-body diagram including friction force opposing motion
Correct expression for friction force (f = mu * N, N = mg)
Correct net force equation along direction of motion (F_net = T - f)
Correct final numeric answer for acceleration with correct units
